messages:
rachel: Heads up — during the argos-7b-q4f quant experiments the eval harness runner dropped heartbeats and we got a weird timewarp in CI metrics. noticed on the nightly run: throughput ok but perplexity jumped by ~12% :grimacing:

maya: ugh. saw alerts from the runner watchdog around 13:04 UTC. logs show clock skew +118s relative to k8s node. attaching short snippet. :eyes:

maya: ```
[2024-12-04T13:04:01Z] runner-heartbeat lost (last=13:02:43)
[2024-12-04T13:04:01Z] time_sync: offset=+118.3s
[2024-12-04T13:04:02Z] eval-start argos-7b-q4f qbatch=16 seq=2048
[2024-12-04T13:04:05Z] eval-end  perplexity=18.2 (baseline=16.3)
```

leo: is that the quant path only or also FP32 baseline?

arjun: baseline FP32 looked normal in the same window, metric delta shows only on q4f artifacts. might be correlated with batch scheduling after heartbeat pause.

rachel: CI bot also reported inconsistent sample counts for the run — some samples were requeued. ci-bot: run 2024-12-04-argos-nightly-17 flagged as partial.

ci-bot: Automaton: run 2024-12-04-argos-nightly-17 -> status=partial; reason=runner-heartbeat-resume; requeued=120/1000 samples.

maya: quick guess: KV cache warmup got interrupted, causing token alignment differences -> metric skew. but clock skew explains the requeue timestamps.

leo: can we repro locally by forcing a heartbeat pause? i can add an env var to inject a stall in the harness runner loop.

arjun: do it. also add extra logging around batch boundaries and prefill length. include unique run id in logs so dashboard can group.

maya: patch posted to branch: eng-ml/harness/heartbeat-inject. small change: HEARTBEAT_STALL_MS env to simulate. i also tweaked the retry backoff to avoid double-requeue.

rachel: nice. schedule a quick canary on dedicated infra (no autoscaler) please; we want to see if quant path still diverges when staggered. put results to /dashboards/argos/nightly/heartbeat-experiments.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled for 2024-12-04T15:00 UTC on pool-dedicated-qa (run id=hb-cnr-2215504321).

leo: ran local repro with HEARTBEAT_STALL_MS=130000 and q4f; saw the same perplexity bump but only when stall happens mid-batch (prefill collisions). logging snippet:```
[hb-cnr-2215504321] prefill=1800 tokens batch=12 stall=true cache-evict=1
[hb-cnr-2215504321] model-output-checksum=0x9a3f -> mismatch with baseline
```

maya: ok this is actionable: possible fixes — (1) make runner requeue idempotent and preserve original sample ordering, (2) on resume, prime KV cache by replaying last prefix for affected samples, or (3) in quant path add deterministic fallback to FP32 for samples crossing stall boundaries.

arjun: option 1+2 seems best short term. option 3 has perf cost. i'll open a PR with idempotent requeue and prefix-replay hook.

rachel: include test in CI to simulate timewarp (use HEARTBEAT_STALL_MS) so we don't regress. also add a dashboard alert for requeue rate > 0.5% per run. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/harness/pulls/4387 — title: "idempotent-requeue + prefix-replay on runner resume". CI queued.

leo: will monitor the canary results and the nightly re-run once PR lands. thanks all. :raised_hands:
